newsitem.title: FRANCE: France may freeze 20 bln Ffr spending - paper.
newsitem.headline: France may freeze 20 bln Ffr spending - paper.

text.p: The French government has drawn up informal plans to freeze 20 billion francs of spending budgeted for 1997 as a reserve against probable overspending in some quarters, newspaper La Tribune reported on Wednesday.
"As in 1995 and 1996, this procedure right at the start of the year is meant to put some credit lines in reserve against an overshoot which is already expected in some areas," it said.
No official comment was immediately available.
The 1997 budget caps spending around 1996 levels to help meet France's target of reducing deficits to three percent of GDP, the level needed to qualify for a single European currency.
This year is the key period for deciding which countries join the common currency, scheduled to start up in 1999.
